'''Bobby Allen Howard''' (born June 1, 1964) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) from 1986 to 1988. He played [[college football]] for the [[Indiana Hoosiers football|Indiana Hoosiers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HowaBo00.htm |title=Bobby Howard Stats |publisher=Pro-Football-Reference.com |access-date=2018-12-23}}</ref>

Howard was a 3-sport standout at [[Langley High School (Pittsburgh)|Langley High School]] in [[Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania]].  As a junior, he ran for over 1,000 yards and scored ten [[touchdowns]] in football, averaged 10 points and 11 [[rebounds]] for the basketball team which made the state playoffs, and had a .540 [[batting average]] for the baseball team.<ref>{{cite news|title=Few Excel Like Star at Langley |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/129109926/ |newspaper=[[The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |date=August 28, 1981 |pages=13 |via = [[Newspapers.com]]|accessdate = July 29, 2023}}</ref>  In his senior year, the Langley baseball team won the city championship, with Howard batting .619.<ref>{{cite news|title=Langley Captures City Title |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/129110607/ |newspaper=[[The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |date=June 2, 1982 |pages=12 |author=Steve Hecht |via = [[Newspapers.com]]|accessdate = July 29, 2023}}</ref>  After graduating, Howard attended [[Indiana University Bloomington]], where he was the No. 3 [[Halfback (American football)|tailback]] as a freshman.<ref>{{cite news|title=How Good Are Hoosiers? |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/129110809/ |newspaper=[[The Indianapolis News]] |date=September 21, 1982 |pages=23 |author=Zach Dunkin |via = [[Newspapers.com]]|accessdate = July 29, 2023}}</ref> In his senior year he was named to [[United Press International|UPI]]'s second team all-[[Big Ten]] conference.<ref>{{cite news|title=IU's Bobby Howard Listed on the Second team |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/129111114/ |newspaper=[[The Reporter-Times]] |date=November 26, 1985 |pages=9 |author=Randy Minkoff |via = [[Newspapers.com]]|accessdate = July 29, 2023}}</ref>  He was voted the team's most valuable player, and gained 967 yards during the season.  In April 1986, Howard was selected by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in the 12th round of the [[1986 NFL draft]], the 325th overall pick in the draft.<ref>{{cite news|title=Indiana's Steve Bradley Gets Late Call By Cincinnati |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/129111581/ |newspaper=[[The South Bend Tribune]] |date=April 30, 1986 |pages=11 |author=Randy Minkoff |via = [[Newspapers.com]]|accessdate = July 29, 2023}}</ref>  After a promising start with the Eagles where he was slated to be on the first team, he was cut during pre-season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Eagles Place E. Jackson On Waivers |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/129112103/ |newspaper=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |date=September 17, 1986 |pages=76 |via = [[Newspapers.com]]|accessdate = July 29, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Ryan Needs Wins to Match Words |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/129112225/ |newspaper=[[Philadelphia Daily News]] |date=September 4, 1986 |pages=111 |via = [[Newspapers.com]]|accessdate = July 29, 2023}}</ref>  In October 1986 he was signed by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{cite news|title=NFL Moves |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/129112338/ |newspaper=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |date=October 29, 1986 |pages=38 |via = [[Newspapers.com]]|accessdate = July 29, 2023}}</ref>

'''Bobby Brown III''' (born August 7, 2000) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive tackle]] for the [[Carolina Panthers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas A&M Aggies football|Texas A&M Aggies]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zwerneman |first=Brent |date=April 28, 2021 |title=Texas A&M's Bobby Brown isn't shy on draft prospects |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/Texas-A-M-s-Bobby-Brown-isn-t-shy-on-draft-16137017.php |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=Houston Chronicle}}</ref> He was selected by the [[Los Angeles Rams]] in the fourth round of the [[2021 NFL draft]].

==College career==
He played college football at [[Texas A&M Aggies football|Texas A&M]] from 2018 to 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Brown III - Football |url=https://12thman.com/sports/football/roster/bobby--brown-iii/7943 |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=Texas A&M Athletics - 12thMan.com |language=en}}</ref> He ranked seventh in the [[Southeastern Conference]] with 5.5 sacks in the 2020 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2020 Southeastern Conference Leaders |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfbconferences/sec/2020-leaders.html |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Rams===
Brown was selected by the [[Los Angeles Rams]] in the fourth round, 117th overall, of the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Stu |date=May 1, 2021 |title=Rams select DT Bobby Brown III with 117th pick |url=https://www.therams.com/news/bobby-brown-iii-nfl-draft-defensive-tackle-texas-am |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=TheRams.com}}</ref> He signed his four-year rookie contract with the Rams on June 3, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Levine |first=Ben |date=June 3, 2021 |title=Rams Sign Fourth-Round DL Bobby Brown III |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2021/06/rams-sign-fourth-round-dl-bobby-brown-iii |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=Pro Football Rumors |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=February 13, 2022 |title=Los Angeles Rams win Super Bowl LVI |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/super-bowl-lvi-what-we-learned-from-rams-win-over-bengals |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Brown ended his rookie season with a Rams [[Super Bowl LVI]] victory against the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LVI - Los Angeles Rams vs. Cincinnati Bengals - February 13th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202202130cin.htm |access-date=March 25, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Brown was suspended the first six games of the 2022 season for violating the NFL’s policy on performance-enhancing substances.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |date=July 18, 2022 |title=Bobby Brown suspended six games |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2022/07/18/bobby-brown-suspended-six-games/ |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=ProFootballTalk |publisher=NBC Sports}}</ref> In the 2022 season, he appeared in nine games and started one. He finished with eight total tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Brown 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrowBo04/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On October 10, 2023, Brown was placed on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Grindley |first=Wyatt |date=October 10, 2023 |title=Rams Place NT Bobby Brown On IR |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/rams-place-nt-bobby-brown-on-ir/ |access-date=October 22, 2023 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co |language=en-US}}</ref> He was activated on November 18.<ref name="c010">{{cite web | last=DaSilva | first=Cameron | title=Rams activate Bobby Brown III off injured reserve | website=Rams Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=November 18, 2023 | url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/2023/11/18/rams-activate-bobby-brown-iii-off-injured-reserve/ | access-date=December 10, 2024}}</ref> In the 2023 season, he appeared in and started 13 games. He had a half-sack and 31 tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Brown 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrowBo04/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=January 8, 2025 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2024 season, he appeared in all 17 games and started 16. He finished with 44 tackles and one pass defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobby Brown 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrowBo04/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=January 19, 2025 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
On March 14, 2025, Brown signed a three-year, $21 million contract with the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/article/bobby-brown-iii-heads-to-panthers-on-a-3-year-21-million-deal-report-212410073.html|title=Bobby Brown III heads to Panthers on a 3-year, $21 million deal: Report|work=Yahoo.com|first=Ryan|last=Young|date=March 10, 2025|accessdate=March 14, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/being-bobby-brown-iii-a-long-night-s-journey-into-a-new-day|work=Panthers.com|title=Being Bobby Brown III: A long night's journey into a new day|date=March 14, 2025|first=Darin|last=Gantt|accessdate=March 14, 2025}}</ref>

Bell is the son of former [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] player [[Bobby Bell]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://newspapers.com/article/lincoln-journal-star/134590070/|newspaper=[[Lincoln Journal Star]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=October 10, 1983|page=14|title=An All-Pro, proud father|author=Babcock, Mike}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://newspapers.com/article/st-louis-post-dispatch/134590117/|newspaper=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=November 12, 1982|page=13|title=Bobby Bell's Legacy Lives With His Son|author=Smith, Mike}} {{Open access}}</ref>

'''Bobby Lane Fowler''' (born September 11, 1960) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]] for one season with the [[New Orleans Saints]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played  [[college football]] for the [[UTEP Miners football|UTEP Miners]] and [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football|Louisiana Tech Bulldogs]].

==Early life and college==
Bobby Lane Fowler was born on September 11, 1960, in [[Temple, Texas]].<ref name="Pfa">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/f/fowl00800.html | title=Bobby Fowler | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=13 May 2025}}</ref> He attended [[Angleton High School]] in [[Angleton, Texas]].<ref name="Pfa"/>

Fowler first played [[college football]] for the [[UTEP Miners football|UTEP Miners]] of the [[University of Texas at El Paso]].<ref name="Pfa"/> He was a member of the team from 1978 to 1979, earning a [[letterman (sports)|letter]] during the latter season.<ref name="Pfa"/> He then transferred to play for the [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football|Louisiana Tech Bulldogs]] of [[Louisiana Tech University]].<ref name="Pfa"/> Fowler was listed as ineligible in 1981 and was a two-year letterman from 1982 to 1983.<ref name="Pfa"/>

==Professional career==
Fowler signed with the [[New Orleans Saints]] on
June 20, 1984, after going undrafted in the [[1984 NFL draft]].<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/f/fowl00800.html | title=Bobby Fowler Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=13 May 2025}}</ref> He was released on August 27, 1984.<ref name="transactions"/> He signed with the Saints again on May 9, 1985.<ref name="transactions"/> Fowler was placed on injured reserve on 
September 2 and was later activated on October 15, 1985.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in ten games for the Saints during the 1985 season, recording five receptions for 43 yards, two carries for four yards, and four kick returns for 78 yards.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FowlBo20.htm | title=Bobby Fowler | publisher=[[Pro Football Reference]] | accessdate=13 May 2025}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on August 15, 1986, and missed the entire 1986 season.<ref name="transactions"/> Fowler was released by New Orleans on July 27, 1987, after failing a physical.<ref name="transactions"/>
